title: MarkovQuadraticInterpolation.lean

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained convex quadratic minimization: f(x)-f(u)=½⟨x-u,H̄(x-u)⟩, where H̄=Σ_i π_i H_i and 0≤H_i≤LI. Strong convexity is not required.

problem_class.label: finite_sum
problem_class.details: The population objective is a finite, probability-weighted sum of quadratic component losses. The number of components m, weights π, operators H_i, and common minimizer u are hidden.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: Each call at x returns H_i(x-u), with i sampled along an exogenous finite-state Markov chain. Its stationary mean is ∇f(x), but conditional unbiasedness is not assumed. The oracle returns only the gradient vector; component indices and transition information are hidden.

oracle.label: component_gradient
oracle.details: Replies are exact gradients of the sampled quadratic components. The algorithm cannot select the component; consecutive calls advance the Markov trajectory.

distinctive_assumptions.label: markov_dependence
distinctive_assumptions.details: The chain has invariant distribution π and arbitrary initial distribution μ. Its transition kernel satisfies κ(i,{j})≥απ({j}) for every i,j, with public 0<α≤1. Reversibility and stationary initialization are not required.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Exact interpolation: every component gradient vanishes at the same hidden u. Each H_i is bounded, self-adjoint and positive semidefinite, with 0≤⟨x,H_i x⟩≤L‖x‖². The ambient space is a complete real Hilbert space with its Borel measurable structure and second-countable topology. E,L,x0,α are public; R and ε are hidden analysis parameters, with L>0, R≥0, ε>0 and ‖x0-u‖≤R.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/MarkovQuadraticInterpolation.lean: Public, Params, Model.symmetric, Model.positive, Model.smooth, Model.radius, spec.publicInput, spec.valid; LongTails/Setups/SmoothAndConvex.lean: Gradient.Public.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The output must be measurable and have integrable excess objective value relative to a global minimizer u. No last-iterate or averaging restriction is imposed by successful.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: E[f(output)-f(u)]≤ε under the joint algorithm and oracle randomness. Oracle cost is bounded for every seed by the fixed budget ⌈10¹⁶LR²/(αε)⌉+1.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/MarkovQuadraticInterpolation.lean: spec.successful; LongTails/Template.lean: Convergence; supplied extracted budget for OracleTemplate.MarkovQuadratic.result.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: Convex quadratic interpolation is combined with a hidden Markov component-gradient oracle, arbitrary chain initialization, and a public one-step stationary minorization parameter in a potentially infinite-dimensional Hilbert space.

descriptionHtml:
Markov Quadratic Interpolation

We consider minimizing a convex quadratic f:E→R on a separable real Hilbert space E. It is the stationary average of quadratic losses sharing a minimizer x⋆, with positive semidefinite Hessians bounded by L>0. A given point x0∈E satisfies ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R, where R≥0. At query x, the oracle returns HZ(x−x⋆), where HZ is the Hessian indexed by a finite-state Markov chain Z. The chain starts arbitrarily and its transition law dominates α times its invariant law, with 0<α≤1. For ε>0, the goal is E[f(x¯)−f(x⋆)]≤ε, averaging over the chain and independent algorithm randomness for the output x¯∈E.

The optimization problem is minx∈Ef(x). The norm ∥⋅∥ is induced by the inner product on E. The algorithm receives only E, L, x0, and α; the radius R and tolerance ε may enter the oracle-call budget but are not algorithm inputs.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Interpolating quadratic model). There exist a finite index set I={1,…,m} with m≥1, a probability distribution π on I, bounded linear operators Hi:E→E, and a point x⋆∈E such that Hi∗=Hi(i∈I),0≤⟨v,Hiv⟩≤L∥v∥2(i∈I, v∈E),∥x0−x⋆∥≤R. Here Hi∗ denotes the Hilbert space adjoint. The population objective satisfies f(x)−f(x⋆)=12EI∼π[⟨x−x⋆,HI(x−x⋆)⟩],x∈E. In particular, x⋆ is a global minimizer and every component gradient vanishes there.

Assumption 2 (Markov sampling and refresh). Let κ be a Markov transition kernel on I, and write πj=π({j}). Its invariant distribution and refresh condition satisfy EI∼π[κ(I,{j})]=πj(j∈I),κ(i,{j})≥απj(i,j∈I). The samples (Zk)k≥0 form a time-homogeneous Markov chain with transition kernel κ and arbitrary initial distribution μ on I. Algorithm randomness is independent of this chain.

Queries may be made at any point of E. At the kth call, starting with k=0, a query x receives the vector g(x,Zk)=HZk(x−x⋆). Thus successive calls use successive states of the same chain. The distributions π and μ, the kernel κ, the operators Hi, and the minimizer x⋆ are not supplied to the algorithm.

After the allotted oracle calls, the output x¯ must be measurable, its objective gap must be integrable, and it must satisfy E[f(x¯)−f(x⋆)]≤ε.

comparisonHtml:
On a real separable Hilbert space with its Borel measurable structure, let 0⪯Hi⪯LI be self-adjoint operators indexed by a finite state space, with f(x)−f(x⋆)=12∑iπi⟨x−x⋆,Hi(x−x⋆)⟩ and ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R. The oracle returns Hst(x−x⋆) along a Markov chain with stationary law π, arbitrary initial law, and κ(i,⋅)≥απ. Here L>0, R≥0, 0<α≤1, and ε>0. The target is ∫[f(x^)−f(x⋆)]dP≤ε; the setup imposes no algorithm or output-rule restriction.

import LongTails.Setups.SmoothAndConvex
import LongTails.Setups.HeavyTailedMarkovSmoothAndConvex
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Adjoint
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.MeasurableSpace.Instances

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace LongTails.Setups.MarkovQuadraticInterpolation

open OracleTemplate

structure Public extends toGradientPublic : LongTails.Setups.SmoothAndConvex.Public where
  [measurableE : MeasurableSpace E]
  [borelE : BorelSpace E]
  [countableE : SecondCountableTopology E]
  α : ℝ

attribute [instance] Public.measurableE Public.borelE Public.countableE

structure Params extends Public where
  R : ℝ
  ε : ℝ

structure Model (q : Params) (m : ℕ) (π : ProbabilityMeasure (Fin m))
    (κ : Kernel (Fin m) (Fin m)) (H : Fin m → q.E →L[ℝ] q.E)
    (f : q.E → ℝ) (u : q.E) : Prop where
  stationary : κ ∘ₘ (π : Measure (Fin m)) = (π : Measure (Fin m))
  refresh : ∀ i j, ENNReal.ofReal q.α * (π : Measure (Fin m)) {j} ≤ κ i {j}
  symmetric : ∀ i, (H i).adjoint = H i
  positive : ∀ i x, 0 ≤ ⟪x, H i x⟫
  smooth : ∀ i x, ⟪x, H i x⟫ ≤ q.L * ‖x‖ ^ 2
  radius : ‖q.x0 - u‖ ≤ q.R
  population : ∀ x, f x - f u =
    ∫ i, ⟪x - u, H i (x - u)⟫ / 2 ∂(π : Measure (Fin m))

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Public
  Instance q := q.E → ℝ
  Query q := q.E
  Reply q := q.E
  Output q := q.E
  publicInput := Params.toPublic
  valid q := 0 < q.L ∧ 0 ≤ q.R ∧ 0 < q.α ∧ q.α ≤ 1 ∧ 0 < q.ε
  admissible q f O :=
    ∃ (m : ℕ) (π μ : ProbabilityMeasure (Fin m)) (κ : Kernel (Fin m) (Fin m))
      (hκ : IsMarkovKernel κ) (H : Fin m → q.E →L[ℝ] q.E) (u : q.E),
      Model q m π κ H f u ∧
      O = { Seed := fun _ => Fin m
            law := @LongTails.Setups.HeavyTailedMarkovSmoothAndConvex.pathLaw (Fin m) _ κ hκ μ
            answer := fun _ (_, x) i => H i (x - u) }
  successful q f output P :=
    Measurable output ∧ ∃ u, IsMinOn f Set.univ u ∧
      Integrable (fun ω => f (output ω) - f u) (P : Measure _) ∧
      (∫ ω, f (output ω) - f u ∂(P : Measure _)) ≤ q.ε

end LongTails.Setups.MarkovQuadraticInterpolation
